resources.string:
This app is a cryptocurrency CPU miner. Mining runs your processor at full load for as long as it is active: the device will get hot, draw a lot of power, drain the battery quickly, and sustained mining may accelerate battery and hardware wear.

No dev fee: 100% of what you mine goes to the pool and wallet you configure. Nothing is taken automatically. If a maintainer fee is ever added in the future, it will not activate on any installed copy without advance in-app notice first.

You run this app entirely at your own risk. The developers accept no responsibility for any consequences — including hardware damage, battery wear, electricity costs, lost earnings, or your compliance with local laws and pool terms. No warranty of any kind.

Ghuleh Miner is free software under GPL-3.0-or-later, forked from primo-arm-miner (gitlab.com/PrimoLab/primo-arm-miner). Source code: github.com/heather2084/ghuleh-miner — license texts for the bundled components ship inside this APK (assets/licenses).

ALGORITHM — decides which coin you mine: verus → Verus (VRSC), randomx → Monero (XMR), scrypt → Litecoin + Dogecoin (merged mining), sha256d → Bitcoin (BTC). Each algorithm remembers its own pools and thread count, so switching back later restores them.\n\nTHREADS — how many CPU cores mine at once. All cores gives the highest hashrate but the most heat; if the device gets very hot or throttles, try one or two fewer than the core count.

POOL URL — copy it from your pool's getting-started page, e.g. stratum+tcp://host:port. Use stratum+ssl:// to connect over TLS where the pool offers it.

WALLET / USER.WORKER — usually your wallet address, optionally followed by a dot and a worker name to tell your devices apart (wallet.phone1). A few pools use an account username instead of a wallet address.

PASSWORD — almost always just x. Some pools read options from it, like a fixed difficulty.

FAILOVER POOLS — tried in order when the pool above them is unreachable. A blank wallet or password on a failover means "same as the primary".

The miner serves a read-only, ccminer-compatible status API on port 4068 — it\'s what the dashboard on the home page reads.\n\nAllow network monitoring — also lets other devices on your wifi read it (hashrate, shares, temperature) by connecting to this phone\'s IP on port 4068. It is read-only: nothing on the phone can be changed through it. Off = reachable from this phone only.
